headline: $23M Vistula Metropark in design phase — opening target revised to 2028 for Metroparks Toledo's 100th anniversary
paragraphs: Metroparks Toledo is advancing what will become its 20th park: a $23 million riverfront park along Water Street between Olive and Magnolia in the Vistula neighborhood. The Blade reported (April 22) that Metroparks hired a design consultant — the project is now in its design phase. Earlier reporting from March 2026 had suggested some elements could open later in 2026; June 2026 reporting from 13abc and The Blade indicates the target opening has shifted to 2028, timed to coincide with Metroparks Toledo's 100th anniversary.

The park will feature lagoons, fishing and kayaking access, and will connect to the Glass City Riverwalk, extending Toledo's riverfront trail network further into the Vistula Historic District. Located along the Maumee River between Olive and Magnolia Streets — north of the existing pickleball facility — Vistula Metropark will sit adjacent to the proposed soccer stadium site at Vistula and the ongoing Ostrich Towne mixed-use development corridor.
why_it_matters: Public green space is the most consistent leading indicator for private investment in adjacent parcels in Toledo. Expect land-banking activity within a 4–6 block radius of Water Street over the next 12 months.
